reviewMethod: Reviewed 22 remaining Kettlebells, Plate, Bosu Ball and Medicine Ball sources against all 86 available gender/angle clip files, six chronological samples each. Inspected 72 supplemental samples: four 12-frame first-five-second sequences for clean/jerk and four six-frame offset sequences for BOSU support, plate-twist foot placement and fixed-bar support. Total 588 inspected samples. Partner-toss files show the same two-person demonstration for both media genders; do not imply four distinct performances. Corrections describe visible support, load quantity, grip and movement, not recovered provider wording. Retain step counts and existing side/time cues; do not invent angles, repetitions, sets or loading.
databaseStatus: Applied and verified against the live database. Vietnamese coverage is 1859/1946, with 87 unresolved sources. Existing translations, timestamps, media, categories and favorite counts are unchanged.

before.name: Kettlebell Waiters Bow
steps: Place a barbell at about midway up your thigh. Press your quads into the barbell.
Push your hips back while leaving your knees mostly extended. Look for a stretch in your hamstrings.
When you feel the stretch, push your hips forward until you're back in a standing position.

after.name: Kettlebell Waiters Bow
steps: Set a fixed bar at about mid-thigh height and stand with your thighs against it. Hold a kettlebell in each hand with your arms hanging down.
Push your hips back while keeping your knees mostly extended and your back straight. Look for a stretch in your hamstrings.
When you feel the stretch, push your hips forward until you are back in a standing position, keeping the kettlebells in your hands.

evidence.written_source_status: Reviewed captured source instructions. These are editorial corrections from every available source video sequence, not newly retrieved provider wording.
evidence.observation: Both genders hold one kettlebell in each hand while using a fixed bar at thigh height as a reference/support. Keep the bar distinct from the handheld load; add the missing kettlebells and retain the existing hinge/hamstring-stretch/return cues. Do not replace every occurrence of bar with kettlebell.
evidence.sampling: Six chronological samples across the full recorded duration of each available clip; supplemental offset samples and first-five-second sequences inspect missed phases where recorded.

before.name: Kettlebell Upright Row Single
steps: Stand with your feet shoulder width apart holding the kettlebell with both hands in front of your thighs.
Bend forward at the hips bringing the kettlebell to the floor while you slightly bend your knees, keeping your back straight.
Lift the kettlebell upwards towards your chest and lower - repeat.

after.name: Kettlebell Upright Row Single
steps: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding one kettlebell with both hands in front of your thighs.
Keep your torso upright and bend your elbows, leading them up and out to draw the kettlebell toward your chest.
Lower the kettlebell under control to the front of your thighs, then repeat.

before.name: Plate Single Leg Pinch Grip Deadlift
steps: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and facing forwards. Grip the sides of a weight plate with your palms facing down.
Balance on one foot, as you raise the weight keep your arms and back straight, while you bring your other foot back towards the ground
Keep four raised leg straight and in alignment with your back as you lower the plate back down to the starting position.

Hinge forward at your hips to lower the plates, keeping your back straight as your free leg extends behind you in line with your back.

Bring the kettlebells to your shoulders, with your palms facing inward and your elbows bent.

As you press the kettlebells upwards, also push your hips forward to help generate additional power.
Slowly lower the kettlebells back down to the starting position, and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

after.name: Kettlebell Thruster
steps: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a kettlebell in each hand.
Bring the kettlebells to your shoulders, with your palms facing inward and your elbows bent.
Keeping the kettlebells at your shoulders, bend your hips and knees to lower into a squat.
Drive upward by extending your hips and knees, using that momentum to press both kettlebells overhead.
Lower the kettlebells back to your shoulders under control and repeat for the desired repetitions.
